original_excerpt:
From Felsenheld v. United States, 186 U.S. 126, 134 (1902):
"It is within the power of Congress to prescribe that a package of any article which it subjects to a tax, and upon which it requires the affixing of a stamp, shall contain only the article which is subject to the tax."   

From Felsenheld v. United States, 186 U.S. 126, 131–133 (1902):
Holding that under the federal excise taxing power, Congress has full authority to protect the administration and integrity of excise taxation by prohibiting manufacturers from packing or attaching any foreign objects, promotional coupons, tickets, or premium certificates inside stamped packages of tobacco.
fidelity: Quoted clause corresponds with initial-capitalization delimitation noted for 022. Statutory prohibition of packing/attaching/connecting articles or things and coupon application are supported.
scope_note: 'Full authority' must retain reasonable-regulation qualification; statute excepts specified items (e.g. labels/wrappers), so do not summarize as every object without exceptions.
